statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail 21% remains below the block threshold while Stress is elevated on a 19-year-high US 10-year yield and an unresolved hawkish Fed repricing.
recommendation: Tail sits in the watch band, so the deterministic mapping yields WATCH rather than a blocking state. The evidence-based danger window covers the 12:30-15:30 UTC US claims and cash-open sequence, where a renewed bond leg would be the first sign of mean-reversion failure.
headline: Hawkish rate repricing meets a contained Nasdaq-100 pullback from record levels
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed at 30,470.29 on Sep 23, down 0.85%, one session after setting a record close and still roughly 1% below the 30,770.63 52-week high. The driver was duration, not equity structure: the US 10-year yield rose about 16 basis points to 5.11%, a 19-year high, and the 2-year added about 13 basis points to 4.89% after Fed Governor Michael Barr said further policy adjustments are likely to be needed and S&P Global flash PMIs hit multi-year highs with the steepest input-cost growth since October 2022. Market-implied odds for a move at the Oct 27-28 FOMC sit near 71%, with 16 of 18 policymakers signalling at least one further increase before year-end. Overnight, NQ futures trade near 30,582.50, down 0.59%, inside a 30,512.75-30,813.00 range and about 70 points above the low, while the 10-year is broadly unchanged at roughly 5.11-5.12% and the 2-year has eased about one basis point. That combination matters for path risk: the yield level is extreme, but the yield impulse is not currently extending, and VIX closed at 15.18 after a 14.12-15.45 range, so implied volatility is not pricing a pathological path. Latest-session breadth context is delayed and non-real-time, but it was uniformly soft across the seven tracked semiconductors and mixed across megacaps, with GOOGL down 3.80% and AVGO down 2.62% against gains in META and MSFT, which reads as rotation rather than a broad rout. Brent at $103.38 and WTI at $92.36 keep the inflation channel open. No persistent one-way NQ structure, shallow-pullback sequence, or failed-retracement pattern has been observed, so Tail stays in the watch band while Stress carries the elevated macro backdrop. The session's structural checkpoints are the 12:30 UTC jobless claims and current-account release, the 13:30 UTC cash open, and scheduled Fed speakers through the afternoon.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry published Claude assessments. Tail ran 11-15% through the European and early US hours of Sep 23 in a normal-to-mixed regime, then stepped to 25% for the 14:00 UTC hour as the post-PMI bond leg developed, the only blocking-band reading in the window. It held 20-24% through the US afternoon and into the Asian session, eased to 17-19% between 01:00 and 03:00 UTC, printed 22% at 04:00 UTC on a brief trend-down read, and closed the window at 22% for the 06:00 UTC hour. Stress was the more persistent signal, rising from the mid-30s to a 57% peak at 18:00 UTC and holding around 50% overnight. Confidence stayed in the 84-88% band throughout.
outlookSummary: The published path keeps Tail in the watch band for most of the coming 24 hours, peaking at 24% across the 13:00-15:00 UTC cash-open and Fed-speaker window and easing to 19% during the evening and Asian hours. Stress follows the same shape at a higher level, peaking at 57%, because the extreme yield level and the open inflation channel persist regardless of intraday structure. Confidence decays from 86% to 81% across the horizon as the current price-path evidence ages. The forecast assumes the rate-repricing regime remains unresolved; a renewed 10-year push toward the 5.14% 52-week high alongside shallow NQ pullbacks would argue for a higher Tail than published, while a cooling bond market would argue for a lower one.
